calibration.appliesTo: the UNCONTRACTED share of each tranche only
calibration.basis: The commissioning ramp is the one link with an empirical test, and run uncalibrated the chain overstates every reported quarter (+41%, +90%, +64%; mean bias +65%). The correction is regime-aware, because two different things are being modelled: CONTRACTED GPUs bill take-or-pay from customer acceptance and reach full rate on the modelled ramp, whereas UNCONTRACTED capacity has to be SOLD DOWN, which is what the reported quarters actually measure — in 2025 only 11k of IREN's 23k GPUs were under contract. Fitting a single multiple on the uncontracted leg gives 4.4x and cuts mean absolute error to 11.0% with residuals −16%, +16%, −1%. A flat global multiple fits worse (14.1%) and has the wrong physics: it slows down take-or-pay contracts that bill on acceptance. The calibration is in the BASE case. Confound stated: the 23,000-GPU figure of Sep-2025 is announced-and-on-order, not installed-and-commissioned, so part of the miss is fleet timing rather than sell-down speed; both push revenue later and one multiple is the single-parameter expression of it.
calibration.residuals: −16%, +16%, −1% by quarter after calibration (11.0% mean absolute)

companies.narrative: MARA Holdings is a top-tier Bitcoin miner (~72 EH/s, ~1.9 GW of power across 19 sites, 36,303 BTC) repositioning its power-rich, largely-owned portfolio into an AI/HPC landlord — building powered data-center shells (Long Ridge OH 505MW gas plant + up to 600MW DC; MPLX West Texas 400MW→1.5GW; a Starwood JV targeting ~1GW near-term to >2.5GW) to lease to investment-grade AI/IT tenants while flexing workloads back to mining when economics favor it. companies.narrative: TeraWulf is a Bitcoin miner that has pivoted decisively into AI/HPC colocation landlord — it builds powered data-center shells at Lake Mariner (NY) and Abernathy (TX) and leases them to tenants (Core42, Fluidstack) who bring their own GPUs, with Google backstopping ~$3.2B of Fluidstack's lease obligations and holding ~14% pro forma. In Q1 2026 HPC lease revenue ($21M) surpassed mining for the first time, and the company carries a large contracted book (~$12.8B incl. extensions) plus a ~2.2 GW owned, mostly-uncontracted pipeline (Muskie KY 1GW+, Lake Hawkeye, Chesapeake). The thesis is a re-rate from miner to long-duration power/colocation landlord, financed by debt rather than dilution.
bull: Hyperscaler-grade validation: Google ~$3.2B backstop + ~14% equity stake de-risks Fluidstack lease credit and lowers project financing cost
Large signed, long-dated book — Lake Mariner ~360MW (Core42 + Fluidstack 10yr) plus Abernathy 168MW (25yr) = ~$12.8B contracted incl. extensions
Owned freehold land + secured power across ~2.8 GW portfolio (incl. 1GW+ Muskie KY in cheap-power region) gives durable optionality at low implied $/MW
Financing carried by debt/backstops, not equity — limited dilution relative to scale; HPC revenue already exceeds mining
bear: ~$2.7B net debt and a capital-intensive buildout; revenue ramp is back-end-loaded (most contracted MW energize H2-2026, Muskie not until 2028-2030)
Heavy customer concentration in Fluidstack — a thinly-capitalized neocloud whose lease credit leans on Google's backstop rather than its own balance sheet
~2.2 GW of pipeline (Muskie Ph II, Lake Hawkeye, Chesapeake) is uncontracted and partly speculative; leasing risk on the back half of the stack
